title: Standardization of PCR-RFLP for the molecular characterization of Blastocystis spp. genotypes in human fecal samples
author: maria Alejandra Vethencourt Ysea
license_note: figshare article detail endpoint license.name: CC BY 4.0

steps.instruction: Blastocystis spp. represents the only Stramenopile infecting the human intestine, exhibiting significant genetic diversity despite its morphological pleomorphism. While twenty-eight subtypes (STs) have been identified, ST1–ST4 are the most prevalent in humans and are often associated with clinical symptoms. This study aimed to standardize a PCR-RFLP method for the genetic characterization of these subtypes in human fecal samples. A descriptive study was conducted on 42 individuals positive for Blastocystis spp. referred for parasitological evaluation. Samples were analyzed using direct microscopy, concentration techniques, and culture in modified Boeck-Drbohlav medium. To optimize molecular detection, three DNA extraction methods (Wizard®, Wizard Genomic®, and DNAzol®) were compared. The 18S SSU rRNA gene was targeted through standardized PCR assays, and genetic variability was assessed via RFLP using Hinf I and Rsa I restriction enzymes. Results indicated that the Wizard® method provided the highest-quality DNA from washed cultures. Amplification efficiency was significantly better in cultures (87.5%) and washed stool samples (68.2%) compared to whole stool. RFLP analysis identified single-subtype infections in 85% of the samples, with ST1 (45%) being the most frequent, followed by ST3 (30%) and ST4 (10%); mixed infections were found in 15% of cases.In conclusion, the standardized PCR-RFLP protocol provides a reliable and cost-effective approach for characterizing prevalent Blastocystis subtypes. These findings support the implementation of molecular tools in resource-limited settings to enhance epidemiological research.
